newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles Controller defends airport transfer.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles Controller defends airport transfer.

text.p: Los Angeles City Controller Rick Tuttle said Monday he would stand by his decision to transfer $31 million from the airport to the city's general fund despite criticism by a U.S. senator.

"These are monies that are owed to the taxpayers of the city," Tuttle said. "Efforts to link it to other appropriations or to future airport funding is inappropriate. It's money we're owed and entitled to."

Earlier Monday, Sen. John McCain, R-Ariz., released a two-page letter to Los Angeles Mayor Richard Riordon, charging that the mayor improperly diverted U.S. funds targeted for Los Angeles International Airport to pay city police and firefighters and other bills.

Tuttle maintains the $31 million was repayment for past investments by the city in the airport. The investments were for fire safety and certain public works projects. Tuttle said the city's attorneys had approved the legality of the move.
McCain said if Los Angeles does not return the $31 million, he will push to have the city's federal airport funding slashed by that amount.
"To make these threats are inappropriate," Tuttle said. "As far as using the money and moving forward, that's my view. We should move forward."
